claims.text: The as-cast/solutionized HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The as-cast/solutionized HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The as-cast/solutionized HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
The proposed intervention is aging at approximately 900 °C for 1 hour in an inert atmosphere followed by rapid quenching.
The proposed aging treatment will induce HfC precipitation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The induced HfC precipitates will be uniformly distributed and 10–50 nm in size.
The HfC precipitates will be embedded throughout the refractory-alloy matrix.
Nanoscale HfC precipitates will act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Obstacle interactions with HfC precipitates will force dislocation pile-ups.
The precipitate-induced dislocation interactions will enhance dynamic strain hardening.
Increased work hardening will delay the onset of adiabatic shear banding.
Increased work hardening will improve the uniform distribution of plastic strain during high-strain-rate loading.
Delayed shear localization will postpone dynamic failure.
The precipitate-mediated deformation mechanism will moderate impact-induced energy release.
The prediction is scoped to adiabatic dynamic compression at strain rates from 10^3 to 10^4 s^-1.
The modified alloy will exhibit a 10–15% increase in yield strength relative to the baseline.
The modified alloy's uniform-deformation regime will extend from a stated baseline of 13.5% to approximately 17–18% strain.
The modified alloy will have improved resistance to shear localization.
The modified alloy will exhibit more controlled impact-induced energy release than the baseline.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% baseline value is identified as fracture strain in the initial-state and baseline fields but is treated as the baseline uniform-deformation limit in the predicted outcome. These are not necessarily the same mechanical metric.

The nominal starting alloy lists no carbon, while heat treatment alone is asserted to generate HfC precipitates without specifying an initial carbon content, carbon-bearing phase, or carbon-introduction step.
